feedback: Expected result: you no longer see the light. Light travels in straight lines, so it passes through all three holes only when they are lined up; it cannot bend to reach the offset middle hole.
If a learner predicts the light still gets through (light 'finds its way' or curves round), run the demo so the failure is seen, then link it to why shadows have the same outline as the object.
If a learner says 'you'd still see it because light is everywhere in the room anyway', revisit the beam-in-dust observation to separate light that has landed from light still travelling.
On the dust question: you are seeing the dust scattering the light into your eye, not light that is simply 'everywhere' — the visible beam marks the straight path the light is travelling along.
activities.intendedInsight: Light reaches the eye only when the holes are lined up; the offset-hole result contradicts a 'light bends to find its way' model and supports the model that light travels in straight lines.
learnerActions: Line up three cards, each with a small hole punched in the middle, and shine a torch so light passes through all three holes to your eye (threading string through the holes helps show the straight line).
Before moving anything, predict: if you slide the MIDDLE card sideways, will you still see the light? Say why first.
Slide the middle card off-line and check your prediction.
Explain what the result proves about how light travels.
Discuss: when you see the beam in dusty air, are you seeing the light itself or the dust it lights up?
activities.title: Three holes in a line — predict, then break the alignment

feedback: If a learner expects to see round the bend, have them trace the straight tube with a ruler or string to show the sightline cannot curve.
Connect back: the same straightness is why shadows have the object's outline and why the three holes must align.
activities.intendedInsight: Because light travels in straight lines from an object to your eye, you cannot see round a corner without something like a mirror to redirect the light.
learnerActions: Hold a rolled tube to your eye and confirm you can only see what is straight ahead through it.
Try to use the tube to see something off to one side, around a corner — and find you cannot.
Explain how this shows that light travels in straight lines from an object to your eye.
activities.title: You can't see round corners
